```text
  "body": "## User Story\n\nAs an attendee of a multi-seat event, I want to join a waitlist when every seat is taken and be offered a seat when one becomes available, so that I don't have to keep checking the booking page.\n\n## User Scenario\n\nA host runs a 30-minute class with two seats. Attendees A and B book the 10:00 session. Attendee C opens the booking page, sees the \"Join waitlist\" option just as they would for a fully booked regular event, and joins.\n\nLater, Attendee A cancels their seat while Attendee B remains booked. Attendee C receives an email notifying them that a seat is available, and one seat is held for them for six hours. Attendee C follows the claim link and completes their booking. Attendee C is added to the existing booking without affecting Attendee B's booking.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n### Joining the Waitlist\n\n- [ ] Fully booked multi-seat times display the existing \"Join waitlist\" button using the same appearance, placement, and registration form as regular single-attendee events.\n- [ ] Multi-seat times with at least one available seat continue displaying their usual seat availability without a waitlist option.\n- [ ] Days where every multi-seat time is full display the existing \"Join waitlist for this day\" option.\n- [ ] For multi-seat events, `GET /api/waitlist/booked-times` returns only times where every seat is booked.\n- [ ] `POST /api/waitlist` creates a `WAITING` entry for a fully booked multi-seat time or day and rejects specific-time registrations for times with available seats with a 400 error.\n\n### Offers and Seat Holds\n\n- [ ] Cancelling an individual seat while other attendees remain booked queues an `offerWaitlistSpot` task for that time.\n- [ ] Available seats for waitlist offers are calculated as `seatsPerTimeSlot - booked attendees - active offers`.\n  - Active offers are unexpired `OFFERED` entries whose attendees have not yet booked.\n  - Successfully claimed offers are counted only as booked attendees, preventing double-counting.\n  - No offers are sent when available capacity is zero or less.\n  - For example, an event with three seats, one booked attendee, and one active offer has one remaining seat available to offer. After the active offer is claimed, two attendees are booked, zero active offers remain, and one seat is still available.\n- [ ] When multiple seats become available, eligible waitlisted attendees receive offers in oldest-first order, up to the available capacity.\n- [ ] Each waitlist hold reserves exactly one seat (`isSeat: true`) without blocking other available seats.\n\n### Claiming an Offered Seat\n\n- [ ] The claim link opens the booking page with the offered time selected and displays the reserved seat as available to the claimant.\n- [ ] Claiming a seat adds the attendee to the existing booking or creates a booking if none exists, without affecting other attendees' records, seats, or booking status.\n- [ ] After a successful booking, the corresponding waitlist hold is released immediately so that seat availability is accurate and the seat is not counted twice.\n- [ ] When an offer expires:\n  - If the waitlisted attendee has booked, the entry becomes `CLAIMED`.\n  - If no seat remains available, the entry returns to `WAITING`.\n  - If the seat remains available, the entry becomes `EXPIRED`, and the next eligible attendee receives an offer.\n\n### Testing and Regression\n\n- [ ] Existing six-hour waitlist rules and single-attendee event behavior remain unchanged.\n- [ ] Automated tests cover waitlist registration, seat cancellations, capacity calculations, seat holds, successful claims, and offer expiration.\n- [ ] Relevant regression tests and TypeScript type-checking pass.\n- [ ] Manual testing verifies the complete multi-seat waitlist flow, from registration to claiming a freed seat, without affecting existing attendees or displaying incorrect seat availability.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Waitlist offers triggered by rescheduling.\n- Email delivery failures and retries.\n- Existing general duplicate-offer race conditions.\n- Enforcing waitlist holds on bookings made directly through the API.\n- Host waitlist management controls, including per-event toggles, waitlist size limits, and viewing waiting attendees.\n- Round-robin events where multiple hosts are booked at the same time.\n\n## Open Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Design Decisions\n\n### Capacity-aware waitlist offers\n\n**Alternatives considered:**\n- Offer only one seat at a time, regardless of how many seats are available.\n- Offer multiple seats based on the event's capacity, existing bookings, and active unclaimed offers.\n\n**Chosen approach:**\n\nUse capacity-aware offers to notify eligible waitlisted attendees based on the number of available seats.\n\n**Rationale:**\n\nThis respects multi-seat event capacity, allows multiple available seats to be filled, and prevents successfully claimed offers from being counted twice.\n\n### Seat-level reservations\n\n**Alternatives considered:**\n- Reserve the entire time slot when a waitlist offer is sent.\n- Reserve only one seat per waitlist offer using the existing `isSeat` functionality.\n\n**Chosen approach:**\n\nReserve one seat per offer and release the corresponding hold after a successful booking.\n\n**Rationale:**\n\nThis preserves availability for other attendees, prevents unnecessary blocking of the entire time slot, and reuses existing reservation functionality without requiring database schema changes.\n\n## Related Issues\n\n- Follow-up to #13 and PR #125.\n",
```

```text
    29	export class WaitlistService {

    36	  /** `date` is YYYY-MM-DD in the booker's `timeZone`; `slotStart` narrows the entry to one specific time. */
    37	  async join(input: {
    38	    eventTypeId: number;
    39	    name: string;
    40	    email: string;
    41	    timeZone: string;
    42	    date: string;
    43	    slotStart?: Date;

    45	    const dayStart = dayjs.tz(input.date, input.timeZone).startOf("day");
    46	    const dayEnd = dayStart.add(1, "day");
    47	    const slotStart = input.slotStart ?? null;
    48	    if (slotStart && (slotStart < dayStart.toDate() || slotStart >= dayEnd.toDate())) {
    49	      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest("Waitlist time must fall on the selected day");
    50	    }
    51	    const latestStart = slotStart ? slotStart.getTime() : dayEnd.valueOf();
    52	    if (latestStart - this.now() <= WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS) {
    53	      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest("Waitlist is not available less than 6 hours in advance");
    54	    }
    55	
    56	    const eventType = await this.deps.waitlistRepo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(input.eventTypeId);
    57	    if (!eventType) throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.NotFound(`Event type ${input.eventTypeId} not found`);
    58	
    59	    const email = input.email.toLowerCase();
    60	    const existing = await this.deps.waitlistRepo.findWaitingByEmailAndDay({

    62	      email,
    63	      dayStart: dayStart.toDate(),
    64	      slotStart,
    65	    });

    67	
    68	    return this.deps.waitlistRepo.create({

    79	  /** Start times of this event type's bookings that could still be waitlisted (more than 6 hours away). */

    92	  async offerSpot(slot: FreedSlot): Promise<number | null> {
    93	    const now = this.now();

   153	    if (!entry || entry.status !== WaitlistStatus.OFFERED || !entry.offerStart) return;
   154	    // Left over from an offer attempt that was rolled back and re-made later
   155	    if (entry.offerExpiresAt && entry.offerExpiresAt.getTime() > this.now()) return;
   156	
   157	    await repo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
   158	    const bookedEmails = await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt({
   159	      eventTypeId: entry.eventTypeId,
   160	      startTime: entry.offerStart,
   161	    });
   162	    if (bookedEmails) {
   163	      // Someone else booked during the hold: the waitlister keeps their place for the day
   164	      const claimed = bookedEmails.includes(entry.email.toLowerCase());
   165	      await repo.transition(
   166	        entry.id,
   167	        WaitlistStatus.OFFERED,
   168	        claimed ? WaitlistStatus.CLAIMED : WaitlistStatus.WAITING,

   175	      await this.offerToNext(entry);
   176	    }
   177	  }

   180	  async leave(uid: string): Promise<boolean> {
   181	    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
   182	    const entry = await repo.findByUid(uid);
   183	    if (!entry) return false;
   184	
   185	    if (entry.status === WaitlistStatus.WAITING) {
   186	      return repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, WaitlistStatus.LEFT);
   187	    }
   188	    if (entry.status !== WaitlistStatus.OFFERED) return false;
   189	    if (!(await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.LEFT))) return false;

   191	    await repo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
   192	    await this.offerToNext(entry);

   194	  }

   197	  async getClaimUrl(uid: string): Promise<string | null> {

    18	  // The slot hold is keyed by the entry uid; the booker identifies its own holds via the `uid` cookie
    19	  const useSecureCookies = WEBAPP_URL.startsWith("https://");
    20	  response.cookies.set("uid", uid, {
    21	    path: "/",
    22	    sameSite: useSecureCookies ? "none" : "lax",
    23	    secure: useSecureCookies,
    24	  });
    25	  return response;
    26	}
```

```text
    14	  // Padded so leading/trailing days shown from adjacent months and multi-day views are covered
    15	  const from = monthStart.subtract(7, "day").toISOString();
    16	  const to = monthStart.add(1, "month").add(14, "day").toISOString();
    17	
    18	  const { data } = useQuery({
    19	    queryKey: ["waitlist-booked-times", eventId, from, to],
    20	    enabled: !!eventId,
    21	    queryFn: async () => {
    22	      const params = new URLSearchParams({ eventTypeId: String(eventId), from, to });
    23	      const res = await fetch(`/api/waitlist/booked-times?${params.toString()}`);
    24	      if (!res.ok) return [];
    25	      const body: { times: string[] } = await res.json();
    26	      return body.times;
    27	    },
    28	  });
    29	
    30	  return useMemo(() => {
    31	    const byDay: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    32	    for (const time of data ?? []) {
    33	      const day = dayjs(time).tz(timezone).format("YYYY-MM-DD");
    34	      (byDay[day] ??= []).push(time);
    35	    }
    36	    return byDay;
    37	  }, [data, timezone]);
    38	};
```

```text
   331	/** Interleaves booked times (as ISO strings) with open slots in time order, skipping times that are still open. */
   332	const mergeByTime = (slots: Slot[], bookedTimes: string[]): (Slot | string)[] => {
   333	  if (!bookedTimes.length) return slots;
   334	  const openTimes = new Set(slots.map((slot) => dayjs(slot.time).valueOf()));
   335	  const booked = bookedTimes.filter((time) => !openTimes.has(dayjs(time).valueOf()));
   336	  const timeOf = (item: Slot | string) => dayjs(typeof item === "string" ? item : item.time).valueOf();
   337	  return [...slots, ...booked].sort((a, b) => timeOf(a) - timeOf(b));
   338	};
```

```text
    const ownWaitlistHoldUid = bookerClientUid ? getWaitlistHoldUid(bookerClientUid) : undefined;

    );

    await _cleanupExpiredSlots({ eventTypeId });

    const reservedSlots = slotsSelectedByOtherUsers;

    return reservedSlots;

    async function _cleanupExpiredSlots({ eventTypeId }: { eventTypeId: number }) {
      await slotsRepo.deleteManyExpiredSlots({ eventTypeId, currentTimeInUtc });
    }

  private async _getDynamicEventType(
    input: TGetScheduleInputSchema,
    organizationDetails: { currentOrgDomain: string | null; isValidOrgDomain: boolean }
  ) {
    const { currentOrgDomain, isValidOrgDomain } = organizationDetails;
    // For dynamic booking, we need to get and update user credentials, schedule and availability in the eventTypeObject as they're required in the new availability logic
    if (!input.eventTypeSlug) {
      // never happens as it's guarded by our Zod Schema refine, but for clear type safety we throw an Error if the eventTypeSlug isn't given.
      throw new Error("Event type slug is required in dynamic booking.");
    }
    const dynamicEventType = getDefaultEvent(input.eventTypeSlug);

    const userRepo = this.dependencies.userRepo;
    const usersForDynamicEventType = await userRepo.findManyUsersForDynamicEventType({
      currentOrgDomain: isValidOrgDomain ? currentOrgDomain : null,
      usernameList: Array.isArray(input.usernameList)
        ? input.usernameList
        : input.usernameList
          ? [input.usernameList]
          : [],
    });

    const usersWithOldSelectedCalendars = usersForDynamicEventType.map((user) => withSelectedCalendars(user));

    const isDynamicAllowed = !usersWithOldSelectedCalendars.some((user) => !user.allowDynamicBooking);
    if (!isDynamicAllowed) {
      throw new TRPCError({
        message: "Some of the users in this group do not allow dynamic booking",
        code: "UNAUTHORIZED",
      });
    }
    return Object.assign({}, dynamicEventType, {
      users: usersWithOldSelectedCalendars,
    });
```

```text
    if (!bookings) {
      const bookingRepo = this.dependencies.bookingRepo;
      bookings = await bookingRepo.findAllExistingBookingsForEventTypeBetween({
        userIdAndEmailMap: new Map([[userId, userEmail]]),
        eventTypeId,
        startDate: startTimeAdjustedWithMaxBuffer,
        endDate: endTimeAdjustedWithMaxBuffer,
        seatedEvent,
      });
    }

    const bookingSeatCountMap: { [x: string]: number } = {};
    const busyTimes = bookings.reduce((aggregate: EventBusyDetails[], booking) => {
      const { id, startTime, endTime, eventType, title, ...rest } = booking;

      const minutesToBlockBeforeEvent = (eventType?.beforeEventBuffer || 0) + (afterEventBuffer || 0);
      const minutesToBlockAfterEvent = (eventType?.afterEventBuffer || 0) + (beforeEventBuffer || 0);

      if (rest._count?.seatsReferences) {
        const bookedAt = `${dayjs(startTime).utc().format()}<>${dayjs(endTime).utc().format()}`;
        bookingSeatCountMap[bookedAt] = bookingSeatCountMap[bookedAt] || 0;
        bookingSeatCountMap[bookedAt]++;
        // Seat references on the current event are non-blocking until the event is fully booked.
        if (
          // there are still seats available.
          bookingSeatCountMap[bookedAt] < (eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot || 1) &&
          // and this is the seated event, other event types should be blocked.
          eventTypeId === eventType?.id
        ) {
          // then we ONLY add the before/after buffer times as busy times.
          if (minutesToBlockBeforeEvent) {
            aggregate.push({
              start: dayjs(startTime).subtract(minutesToBlockBeforeEvent, "minute").toDate(),
              end: dayjs(startTime).toDate(),
              title: "busy_time.buffer_time",
              source: "Buffer Time for seated event (before)",
            });
          }
          if (minutesToBlockAfterEvent) {
            aggregate.push({
              start: dayjs(endTime).toDate(),
              end: dayjs(endTime).add(minutesToBlockAfterEvent, "minute").toDate(),
              title: "busy_time.buffer_time",
              source: "Buffer Time for seated event (after)",
            });
          }
          return aggregate;
        }
        // if it does get blocked at this point; we remove the bookingSeatCountMap entry
        // doing this allows using the map later to remove the ranges from calendar busy times.
        delete bookingSeatCountMap[bookedAt];
      }
      // rescheduling the same booking to the same time should be possible. Why?
      if (rest.uid === rescheduleUid) {
        return aggregate;
      }
    };
  }

    const { schedulingType, hosts, id } = eventType;
    const hostEmails = hosts?.map((host) => host.user.email);
    const isTeamEvent =
      schedulingType === SchedulingType.MANAGED ||
      schedulingType === SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN ||
      schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE;

    const bookings = await this.dependencies.bookingRepo.findAcceptedBookingByEventTypeId({
      eventTypeId: id,
      dateFrom: dateFrom.format(),
      dateTo: dateTo.format(),
    });

    return bookings.map((booking) => {
      const attendees = isTeamEvent
        ? booking.attendees.filter((attendee) => !hostEmails?.includes(attendee.email))
        : booking.attendees;

      return {
        uid: booking.uid,
        startTime: booking.startTime,
        _count: {
          attendees: attendees.length,
        },
      };
    });
  }

  getCurrentSeats = withReporting(this._getCurrentSeats.bind(this), "getCurrentSeats");
```

```text
/**
 * Takes care of creating/rescheduling non-recurring, non-instant bookings. Such bookings could be TeamBooking, UserBooking, SeatedUserBooking, SeatedTeamBooking, etc.
 * We can't name it CoreBookingService because non-instant booking also creates a booking but it is entirely different from the regular booking.
 * We are open to renaming it to something more descriptive.
 */
export class RegularBookingService implements IBookingService {
  constructor(private readonly deps: IBookingServiceDependencies) {}

  async fireBookingEvents({
    booking,
    organizerUser,
    hashedLink,
    isDryRun,
    bookerEmail,
    bookerName,
    originalRescheduledBooking,
    isRecurringBooking,
    tracingLogger,
  }: {
    booking: {
      id: number;
      uid: string;
      startTime: Date;
      endTime: Date;
      status: BookingStatus;
      userId: number | null;
      userUuid: string | null;
      userEmail: string | null;
    };
    organizerUser: { id: number; uuid: string };
    hashedLink: string | null;
    isDryRun: boolean;
    bookerEmail: string;
    bookerName: string;
    originalRescheduledBooking: BookingType | null;
    isRecurringBooking: boolean;
    tracingLogger: ReturnType<typeof distributedTracing.getTracingLogger>;
  }) {
    try {
      const bookingCreatedPayload = buildBookingCreatedPayload({
        booking,
        organizerUserId: organizerUser.id,
        organizerUserUuid: organizerUser.uuid,
        hashedLink,
        isDryRun,
      });

      const bookingEventHandler = this.deps.bookingEventHandler;

      if (!isRecurringBooking) {
        if (originalRescheduledBooking) {
          const bookingRescheduledPayload: BookingRescheduledPayload = {
            ...bookingCreatedPayload,
            oldBooking: {
              uid: originalRescheduledBooking.uid,
              startTime: originalRescheduledBooking.startTime,
              endTime: originalRescheduledBooking.endTime,
            },
          };
          await bookingEventHandler.onBookingRescheduled({
            payload: bookingRescheduledPayload,
          });
        } else {
          await bookingEventHandler.onBookingCreated({
            payload: bookingCreatedPayload,
          });
        }
      }
    } catch (error) {
      tracingLogger.error("Error while firing booking events", safeStringify(error));
    }
  }

  async createBooking(input: { bookingData: CreateRegularBookingData; bookingMeta?: CreateBookingMeta }) {
    return handler.bind(this)(
      {
        bookingData: input.bookingData,
        ...input.bookingMeta,
      },
      this.deps
    );
  }

  async rescheduleBooking(input: { bookingData: CreateRegularBookingData; bookingMeta?: CreateBookingMeta }) {
    return handler.bind(this)(
      {
        bookingData: input.bookingData,
        ...input.bookingMeta,
      },
      this.deps
    );
  }

  /**
   * @deprecated Exists only till API v1 is removed.
   */
  async createBookingForApiV1(input: {
    bookingData: CreateRegularBookingData;
    bookingMeta?: CreateBookingMeta;
    bookingDataSchemaGetter: BookingDataSchemaGetter;
  }) {
    return handler.bind(this)(
      {
        bookingData: input.bookingData,
        ...input.bookingMeta,
      },
      this.deps,
      input.bookingDataSchemaGetter
    );
  }
}
```

```bash
  async getBookedTimes(input: { eventTypeId: number; from: Date; to: Date }): Promise<Date[]> {
    const earliest = new Date(this.now() + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
    const from = input.from > earliest ? input.from : earliest;
    if (from >= input.to) return [];
    return this.deps.waitlistRepo.findActiveBookingStartTimes({
      eventTypeId: input.eventTypeId,

      to: input.to,
    });

new_bt='''  /**
   * Start times of this event type's bookings that could still be waitlisted (more than 6 hours away).
   * For seated events, only times with every seat booked.
   */
  async getBookedTimes(input: { eventTypeId: number; from: Date; to: Date }): Promise<Date[]> {
    const earliest = new Date(this.now() + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
    const from = input.from > earliest ? input.from : earliest;
    if (from >= input.to) return [];
    const range = { eventTypeId: input.eventTypeId, from, to: input.to };
    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
    const seats = (await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(input.eventTypeId))?.seatsPerTimeSlot;
    if (!seats) return repo.findActiveBookingStartTimes(range);

    const attendeesByTime = new Map<number, number>();
    for (const { startTime, attendees } of await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeCounts(range)) {
      attendeesByTime.set(startTime.getTime(), (attendeesByTime.get(startTime.getTime()) ?? 0) + attendees);
    }
    return [...attendeesByTime]
      .filter(([, attendees]) => attendees >= seats)
      .map(([time]) => new Date(time));
  }

  /**
   * Seats at `time` not taken by a booking or a live offer. A non-seated event is one seat, taken by any booking.
   * Offers whose waitlister already booked are counted only as bookings.
   */
  private async countOpenSeats(eventTypeId: number, time: Date, seatsPerTimeSlot: number | null) {
    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
    const bookedEmails = await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt({ eventTypeId, startTime: time });
    const booked = new Set(bookedEmails ?? []);
    const bookedSeats = seatsPerTimeSlot ? (bookedEmails?.length ?? 0) : bookedEmails ? 1 : 0;
    const offers = await repo.findOfferedForTime({ eventTypeId, time });
    const now = this.now();
    const liveOffers = offers.filter(
      (offer) =>
        !!offer.offerExpiresAt &&
        offer.offerExpiresAt.getTime() > now &&
        !booked.has(offer.email.toLowerCase())
    ).length;
    return { open: (seatsPerTimeSlot ?? 1) - bookedSeats - liveOffers, booked };
  }
'''
assert old_bt in s; s=s.replace(old_bt,new_bt)

end=s.index('  /** Returns false if the entry is unknown or already finished. */')
new_offer='''  /** Offers each open seat of a freed slot to the longest-waiting people for it and holds one seat per offer. */
  async offerSpot(slot: FreedSlot): Promise<number[]> {
    const now = this.now();
    // A slot starting within the claim window can't be held for the full 6 hours, so it isn't offered
    if (slot.start.getTime() - now < WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS) return [];

    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
    const eventType = await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(slot.eventTypeId);
    if (!eventType) return [];
    const seatsPerTimeSlot = eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot;

    const offered: number[] = [];
    // Recounted every round, so concurrent runs for one slot can't offer more seats than are open
    while ((await this.countOpenSeats(slot.eventTypeId, slot.start, seatsPerTimeSlot)).open > 0) {
      const entry = await repo.findOldestWaitingForTime({ eventTypeId: slot.eventTypeId, time: slot.start });
      if (!entry) break;

      const offerExpiresAt = new Date(now + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
      const won = await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, {
        hostUserId: slot.hostUserId,
        offerStart: slot.start,
        offerEnd: slot.end,
        offerExpiresAt,
      });
      // Another offer grabbed this entry concurrently; give the seat to the next person instead
      if (!won) continue;

      try {
        await repo.createSlotHold({
          uid: entry.uid,
          eventTypeId: slot.eventTypeId,
          userId: slot.hostUserId,
          start: slot.start,
          end: slot.end,
          releaseAt: offerExpiresAt,
          isSeat: !!seatsPerTimeSlot,
        });
        await this.deps.scheduleOfferExpiry(entry.id, offerExpiresAt);
        await this.deps.sendOfferEmail({
          name: entry.name,
          email: entry.email,
          timeZone: entry.timeZone,
          eventTitle: eventType.title,
          offerStart: slot.start,
          offerExpiresAt,
          claimUrl: `${this.deps.webappUrl}/api/waitlist/claim?uid=${entry.uid}`,
          leaveUrl: `${this.deps.webappUrl}/api/waitlist/leave?uid=${entry.uid}`,
        });
      } catch (error) {
        // Undo the offer so the task's retry offers the seat to this same person instead of the next one
        await repo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
        await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, null);
        throw error;
      }
      offered.push(entry.id);
    }
    return offered;
  }

  async expireOffer(entryId: number) {
    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
    const entry = await repo.findById(entryId);
    if (!entry || entry.status !== WaitlistStatus.OFFERED || !entry.offerStart) return;
    // Left over from an offer attempt that was rolled back and re-made later
    if (entry.offerExpiresAt && entry.offerExpiresAt.getTime() > this.now()) return;

    await repo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
    const eventType = await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(entry.eventTypeId);
    const { open, booked } = await this.countOpenSeats(
      entry.eventTypeId,
      entry.offerStart,
      eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot ?? null
    );
    if (booked.has(entry.email.toLowerCase())) {
      await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.CLAIMED);
      return;
    }
    if (open <= 0) {
      // Someone else took the seat during the hold: the waitlister keeps their place
      await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, null);
      return;
    }

    if (await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.EXPIRED)) {
      await this.offerToNext(entry);
    }
  }

  /** Frees the hold of the offer the booker claimed via `uid`, so the booked seat isn't counted twice. */
  async releaseHoldAfterBooking(input: { uid: string; eventTypeId: number; start: Date }) {
    const entry = await this.deps.waitlistRepo.findByUid(input.uid);
    if (
      entry?.status !== WaitlistStatus.OFFERED ||
      entry.eventTypeId !== input.eventTypeId ||
      entry.offerStart?.getTime() !== input.start.getTime()
    ) {
      return;
    }
    await this.deps.waitlistRepo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
  }
```

```text
import prisma, { bookingMinimalSelect } from "@calcom/prisma";
import { credentialForCalendarServiceSelect } from "@calcom/prisma/selects/credential";

export async function getBookingToDelete(id: number | undefined, uid: string | undefined) {
  return await prisma.booking.findUniqueOrThrow({
    where: {
      id,
      uid,
    },
    select: {
      ...bookingMinimalSelect,
      recurringEventId: true,
      userId: true,
      user: {
```

```text
import type { Tasker } from "./tasker";
import { getTasker } from "./tasker-factory";

const globalForTasker = global as unknown as {
  tasker: Tasker;
};

export const tasker = globalForTasker.tasker || getTasker();

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") {
  globalForTasker.tasker = tasker;
}

export default tasker;
import type { z } from "zod";

type BookingAuditTaskConsumerPayload = string;

export type TaskerTypes = "internal" | "redis";

  sendWebhook: string;

  >;

) => Promise<string>;
```

```text
  /**
   * Start times of this event type's bookings that could still be waitlisted (more than 6 hours away).
   * For seated events, only times with every seat booked.
   */
  async getBookedTimes(input: { eventTypeId: number; from: Date; to: Date }): Promise<Date[]> {
    const earliest = new Date(this.now() + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
    const from = input.from > earliest ? input.from : earliest;
    if (from >= input.to) return [];
    const range = { eventTypeId: input.eventTypeId, from, to: input.to };
    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
    const seats = (await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(input.eventTypeId))?.seatsPerTimeSlot;
    if (!seats) return repo.findActiveBookingStartTimes(range);

    const attendeesByTime = new Map<number, number>();
    for (const { startTime, attendees } of await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeCounts(range)) {
      attendeesByTime.set(startTime.getTime(), (attendeesByTime.get(startTime.getTime()) ?? 0) + attendees);
    }
    return [...attendeesByTime]
      .filter(([, attendees]) => attendees >= seats)
      .map(([time]) => new Date(time));
  }

  /**
   * Seats at `time` not taken by a booking or a live offer. A non-seated event is one seat, taken by any booking.
   * Offers whose waitlister already booked are counted only as bookings.
   */
  private async countOpenSeats(eventTypeId: number, time: Date, seatsPerTimeSlot: number | null) {
    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
    const bookedEmails = await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt({ eventTypeId, startTime: time });
    const booked = new Set(bookedEmails ?? []);
    const bookedSeats = seatsPerTimeSlot ? (bookedEmails?.length ?? 0) : bookedEmails ? 1 : 0;
    const offers = await repo.findOfferedForTime({ eventTypeId, time });
    const now = this.now();
    const liveOffers = offers.filter(
      (offer) =>
        !!offer.offerExpiresAt &&
        offer.offerExpiresAt.getTime() > now &&
        !booked.has(offer.email.toLowerCase())
    ).length;
    return { open: (seatsPerTimeSlot ?? 1) - bookedSeats - liveOffers, booked };
  }
```

I've implemented issue #154, but I haven't run anything: no tests, type check, Biome or manual testing. Run these:

```bash
TZ=UTC yarn vitest run packages/features/waitlist/services/WaitlistService.test.ts apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.test.tsx packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/test/handleSeats.test.ts
yarn type-check:ci --force
yarn biome check --write .
```

**What changed (8 files, about 410 added / 110 removed lines including tests):**

- **Counting open seats** ([WaitlistService.ts](packages/features/waitlist/services/WaitlistService.ts)): a new `countOpenSeats` works out `seats − booked attendees − live offers`, as the issue specifies. A live offer is an `OFFERED` entry that hasn't expired and whose person hasn't booked yet. A regular single-attendee event counts as one seat that any booking takes, so its behavior is the same as before.
- **Sending offers:** `offerSpot` now keeps offering seats, oldest waiter first, until none are open, and recounts each time. It returns a list of entry ids instead of a single id or `null`. For seated events each hold takes exactly one seat (`isSeat: true`).
- **When an offer expires:** if the person booked, the entry becomes `CLAIMED`. If every seat is taken, it goes back to `WAITING`. If a seat is still open, it becomes `EXPIRED` and the next person gets an offer.
- **`GET /api/waitlist/booked-times`:** for seated events, it only returns times where every seat is booked.
- **`POST /api/waitlist`:** joining a specific seated time that still has seats now gets a 400.
- **Cancelling one seat** ([handleCancelBooking.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts)): this path used to return before the waitlist step ran. It now queues `offerWaitlistSpot` for that time. I moved the queueing code into a shared `queueWaitlistOffers` helper.
- **Releasing the hold after booking** ([event.ts](apps/web/pages/api/book/event.ts)): the claim link already sets the `uid` cookie to the waitlist entry's id. After a successful booking, the route frees that entry's hold, but only when the booking is for the same event type and offered time. This stops the claimed seat being counted twice.
- **Booking page** ([AvailableTimes.tsx](apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx)): a full seated time that can still be waitlisted shows the existing "Join waitlist" button instead of the disabled "Booking full" button. When every seated time on a day is full, the existing day-level waitlist option appears.
- **Tests:** I updated the existing service tests for the new return type and added 10 seated-event cases covering the issue's checklist. I added 2 UI tests, and the existing seat-cancel test now checks that the offer gets queued.

**What I skipped, and risks:**
- Seat counts use the booking's attendee count. Collective seated events that store hosts as attendees would count them as taken seats. Round-robin was out of scope.
- A dry-run booking made from a claim link would still free the hold early.
- The date picker shows fully booked seated days as normal available days, as it did before. They aren't styled as waitlist-only; clicking one shows the waitlist option.

```text
Sprint 3: Project Development & Testing¶
Nov 3 – Nov 19 · All deliverables due Nov 19, 11:59 PM (mid-sprint check-in due Nov 12) · 100 points (12% of course grade)
Sprint 3 continues the development of your project and puts the focus on testing: how well your tests check what your code is supposed to do. The issue backlog, PR workflow, and general expectations carry forward; see Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 for anything not explicitly changed here. This page covers what is new or different in Sprint 3.
Sprint 3 at a glance
Key dates: Nov 12: check-in + at least one code PR (open or merged) · Nov 19: everything else
Important rules (they cost the most points):
No merge without an approval on the latest commit.
Spec review on the issue, saying what was checked.
Every code PR links its issue.
Real AI logs.
Test Evidence table in every PR; expected values not copied from the code's output.
Mutation testing with a tool, before and after reports committed.
Your team introduces no new test failures; skipped tests and disabled checks need an issue.
Unfamiliar with a term?
Check the Glossary for definitions of terms used throughout this page.
Before you begin¶
Check your AI log setup against the AI Log Instructions before your first session.
Read "Things that must improve" below. These issues were observed in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly.
Record your baseline early (see D8): the test results at your Sprint 2 release tag (-csci435-s2), from CI or by running the relevant test suites locally. It helps you find hardening issues and get the mutation tool running.
Try the mutation testing tool early (see D6), on any existing file in the part of the code you work on. Do not wait until your PRs are ready.
What is new in Sprint 3¶
Mutation testing (D6): a new individual deliverable. It replaces the UML diagrams from Sprint 2.
Test evidence section in every PR description (D4).
Hardening issues: one of your issues may be a hardening issue (D1).
Suite health section in the sprint report (D8).
Mid-sprint check-in requires an open PR (D7), due Nov 12.
Team feature for Sprints 3–4
Each team will be assigned a larger feature that spans Sprints 3 and 4. The instructor or TA will post it as an issue in your team's issue tracker and notify your team when it is posted. You will likely need to split it into sub-issues.
Things that must improve from Sprint 2¶
These issues were observed in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly in Sprint 3.
1. Open PRs early. In Sprint 2, most PRs were opened in the last two days, which left no time for review. In Sprint 3, you need a code PR by the mid-sprint check-in (see D7).
2. Independent approval before merging. A PR is merged only after a teammate approves its latest commit. Merging without an approval, or after pushing new commits since the approval, is not allowed. Once approved, the author may merge. To keep reviews moving, request the review on GitHub and notify your reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours.
3. Spec reviews must be visible and show what was checked. Before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment on the issue itself. The comment states what the reviewer checked: whether each acceptance criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered (and whether they are covered), and whether the scope fits. If the reviewer finds problems, they list them and the author updates the spec. If the spec is good, the reviewer says so and approves, but "Looks good!" with nothing about what was checked is not acceptable.
4. Link PRs and issues. Every code PR must link the issue it addresses, so the PR can be checked against the spec. Use Closes #<issue> in the PR description so the issue closes automatically when the PR is merged, and attach issues and code PRs to the Sprint 3 milestone.
5. AI logs must be real logs. A log shows your prompts and the AI's output (SpecStory format recommended; see the AI Log Instructions). The following are not logs and receive no full credit: summaries of a session, paraphrased prompts, a share link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it. File names must follow YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md. Link the log from the issue or PR it documents.
6. The sprint report must render. Check that tables and links display correctly on GitHub (no escaped \| or \[). Use the Sprint 3 sections, not a copy of a previous report.
Deliverables¶
D1 - Sprint Backlog¶
Same process as Sprint 2 (D1), including the priority on carryovers: unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into your Sprint 3 backlog first, or you document on the issue why they are dropped.

Role

Each CSCI 535 (grad) member

Scope must be justified. Each issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why: which components it touches and how much change you expect. The instructor or TA may reclassify an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.
Hardening issues (optional). One of your issues may be a hardening issue: work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources:
Your baseline run (see D8): failing tests, flaky tests, or broken CI checks on main.
Tech debt your team recorded in the "Introduced" and "Encountered" fields of your Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs.
Known bugs found in reviews, after merging, or by teammates.
The upstream issue tracker, for bugs in the parts of the system your team works on.
A hardening issue is scoped like any other issue (see the scope justification above). It must also include evidence that the problem is fixed:
Bug fix: a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
Flaky test: the root cause, and enough repeated runs of that test before and after the fix to show the change (for example, 20 runs for a unit test or 10 for an E2E test).
Broken or missing CI check: links to CI runs before and after the fix.
Failing tests in the baseline: pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group of failures.
Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause counts as small at most.
Team feature. When the team feature issue is posted (see the box under "What is new in Sprint 3"), split it into sub-issues, each with its own owner, spec (D2), and scope. Link each sub-issue to the feature issue. Sub-issues count toward your scope minimum like any other issue. When the feature is posted, add its sub-issues to your Sprint 3 milestone and adjust your backlog as needed.
Create a Sprint 3 milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues to it.
What to provide in D8 (Sprint report): link to the Sprint 3 milestone and the rationale for your backlog decisions.
D2 - Requirements Specification¶
Same format and requirements as Sprint 1 (D2). Specs must be written and reviewed before coding begins; see item 3 in "Things that must improve" for what counts as a review.
Hardening issues use a bug format (include the observed and expected behaviors, the steps to reproduct the issue, and other details about the issue) when they fix a defect. Otherwise, use a short task format: the problem, the goal, acceptance criteria, and other necessary details.
D3 - Design Decisions¶
Same as Sprint 2 (D3): each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and explains the choice.
D4 - Code Changes and Pull Requests¶
Same workflow as Sprint 2 (D4), including the Tech Debt section. Sprint 3 adds a Test Evidence section to every PR description. It replaces the "how it was tested" part of the description, so you don't write it twice.
```

```text
D6 - Mutation Testing (new)¶
This is a new individual deliverable.
What it is. A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (mutants), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is killed. If all tests pass, the mutant survived: your tests did not notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.
What to do. For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two such issues; your small issue may be one of them):
Run a mutation testing tool on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it equivalent (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines your PR added or changed.
Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
Answer the questions in the template below.
Evidence. Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (StrykerJS: add "json" to reporters; Gremlins: --output=<file>.json; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json and -after.json (.txt for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.
Stack
Tool
TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest (Actual Budget, Cal.diy, Excalidraw, Outline, Gitea frontend)
StrykerJS with the Vitest runner
TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)
StrykerJS with the Jest runner
Go (Gitea backend)
Gremlins or go-mutesting
Set it up early. Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services, and choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits the configuration they used. You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to), as long as you run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.
Common problems to watch for:
The tool stops before mutating. Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any of the selected tests fail, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where your baseline run helps).
Tests run against built code. If your tests run against compiled output (for example, a dist folder) instead of the source, mutants in the source are never seen by the tests. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing, or choose tests that run on source.
Tests need services. Some test suites need a database or another service running. Start them before running the tool.
False survivors. If you limit which tests run (for example, with Vitest's dir option), make sure the tests that cover the mutated files are included. Otherwise, mutants that some test would catch are reported as survived or not covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
Long runs. Mutating only the files changed by your PR keeps run time manageable.
If you are blocked
If you cannot get the tool to run, first ask your teammates: someone may already have a working setup. If you are still stuck, tell the TA as early as possible, with the errors you got and the AI log of what you tried. The TA will help you debug it. If it still cannot be made to work, the TA may approve running the tool on a different issue or a different part of your code instead. Problems reported at the end of the sprint will not excuse a missing D6.
```

```text
# Mutation testing: Issue #138 -- Allow hosts to confirm or reject individual recurring booking occurrences

**PR(s):** [#140](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/140)  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner  **Config:** [stryker.138.config.mjs](../../../stryker.138.config.mjs) + [vitest.stryker-138.config.mts](../../../vitest.stryker-138.config.mts), built on the shared [stryker.config.mjs](../../../stryker.config.mjs) by @zach-short  **Command:** `STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/138-zachbowden-<before|after>.json TZ=UTC nvm exec 22 node_modules/.bin/stryker run stryker.138.config.mjs`
**Reports:** [before](reports/138-zachbowden-before.json) · [after](reports/138-zachbowden-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 50.60% → after 81.71% (covered mutants only: 73.68% → 97.10%)

### Setup notes

- **Only the lines this PR added or changed are mutated.** `stryker.138.config.mjs` lists them as line ranges: the new guard in `confirm.handler.ts`, `findByRecurringEventId` in `BookingRepository.ts`, the new lines in `BookingListItem.tsx`, and all of `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx` and the two `getRecurringOccurrences` files.
- **The test list is explicit.** `vitest.stryker-138.config.mts` names this PR's test files plus `BookingRepository.test.ts`. The shared config's `related: true` would also run every test that imports `BookingRepository`, including unrelated calendar-subscription suites that time out under load. A failure on the unmutated code stops Stryker before it mutates anything.
- **Stryker 10 requires Node 22 or newer;** the machine's default is Node 20, so the run uses `nvm exec 22`.
- **Same mutants in both runs.** Both runs produced 99 mutants at identical locations, so the reports compare one-to-one.

| Survived | 15 | 2 |
| No coverage | 26 | 13 |
| Ignored (static) | 16 | 17 |

No test sent a bulk request whose first booking fails the guard, so applying it to bulk requests went unnoticed. Under the mutant, "Confirm all" on a series whose first booking has ended would be refused. The issue (Q2) says the bulk behaviour must not change. |

| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:32` | "not part of a recurring series" message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Only the error code was asserted. |

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

My tests checked actions, not what the user or caller sees. The handler tests asserted the error code but never the message, which is all an API v2 or email-link caller gets. The dialog tests checked which buttons appear and what they send, but never the date and time AC1 requires, nor the title. Because those tests used dates relative to "now", they could not have asserted a formatted date anyway. The survivors also showed I had only tested the happy path. Nothing covered a booking that doesn't exist, a query with no data, or a bulk request whose first booking is in the past. That last one mattered most. My new guard was meant for single-booking requests, but no test would have caught it also blocking "Confirm all", which the issue says must not change. Finally, the 11 uncovered `BookingRepository` mutants showed that mocking the repository in the handler test meant the real query never ran in any test.

**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**

Not directly: the survivors came from missing assertions, not wrong expected values. They did force me to decide where some expected values come from. The ACs don't specify error wording, so the new message assertions don't copy the strings from the code. They only require that the message names the booking id and the reason (its status, or that it ended), which comes from the project's documented error-handling rule. For the date/time test, I worked out "Wed, 4 Mar 2099" and "10:00am - 10:15am" for 15:00 UTC in New York independently of the component. The date format matches the one the booking list already uses. The two boundary mutants (`<` vs `<=`, `>=` vs `>`) are the opposite case. The AC says "past" but doesn't define the exact ending instant, so no requirement gives an expected value. That's why I classified them as equivalent rather than adding a test pinned to my own choice.

**3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**

I used Claude Code (log linked from PR #140).

- **Configuration:** it applied @zach-short's shared Stryker setup and wrote the issue-specific config. It mutates only this PR's changed line ranges and lists the test files explicitly, because `related: true` would also pull in calendar-subscription tests that time out.
- **Running:** the first run failed because Stryker 10 requires Node 22 and my machine had Node 20; I installed Node 22 with nvm and ran Stryker through it.
- **Analysis and tests:** it drafted the classification of the 15 survivors and the new tests.
- **What I verified:**
  - All 6 selected test files (36 tests) pass before mutation.
  - The before and after reports contain the same 99 mutants at the same locations.
  - Each "test gap" survivor shows as Killed in the after report.
  - The computed scores match Stryker's own summary table (81.71% / 97.10%).
- **What I corrected:** its first estimate counted the schema mutant as killed, but the after report shows it as Ignored (a static mutant with `ignoreStatic` on). This write-up reports it that way.
=====
// Mutation testing for Sprint 3 (D6). Run it on the files your PR changed, never on the whole repo:
//   TZ=UTC yarn stryker run --mutate "path/to/file.ts"
// Set STRYKER_JSON to write the JSON report where the course wants it, for example
//   STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/130-zach-short-before.json
/** @type {import("@stryker-mutator/api/core").PartialStrykerOptions} */
export default {
  testRunner: "vitest",
  plugins: ["@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner"],
  vitest: {
    configFile: "vitest.config.mts",
    // Only the tests that import the mutated file run, which keeps a run to minutes in this monorepo.
    related: true,
  },
  // Not inPlace: in this repo the in-place backup lands inside the project, Vitest then collects the backup
  // copies, and the restore drops the executable bit on scripts. The sandbox copy avoids both. These folders
  // have no unit tests that features or web code import, so leaving them out keeps the copy small.
  // .claude and .cursor hold symlinks to folders, and packages/prisma/.env links to a root .env that may not
  // exist; the sandbox copy fails on all three.
  ignorePatterns: [
```

```text
130 /** Offers each open seat of a freed slot to the longest-waiting people for it and holds one seat per offer. */
131 async offerSpot(slot: FreedSlot): Promise<number[]> {
132 const now = this.now();
133 // A slot starting within the claim window can't be held for the full 6 hours, so it isn't offered
134 if (slot.start.getTime() - now < WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS) return [];
135
136 const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
137 const eventType = await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(slot.eventTypeId);
138 if (!eventType) return [];
139 const seatsPerTimeSlot = eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot;
140
141 const offered: number[] = [];
142 // Recounted every round, so concurrent runs for one slot can't offer more seats than are open
143 while ((await this.countOpenSeats(slot.eventTypeId, slot.start, seatsPerTimeSlot)).open > 0) {
144 const entry = await repo.findOldestWaitingForTime({ eventTypeId: slot.eventTypeId, time: slot.start });
145 if (!entry) break;
146
147 const offerExpiresAt = new Date(now + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
148 const won = await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, {
149 hostUserId: slot.hostUserId,
150 offerStart: slot.start,
151 offerEnd: slot.end,
152 offerExpiresAt,
153 });
154 // Another offer grabbed this entry concurrently; give the seat to the next person instead
155 if (!won) continue;
156
157 try {
158 await repo.createSlotHold({
159 uid: entry.uid,
160 eventTypeId: slot.eventTypeId,
161 userId: slot.hostUserId,
162 start: slot.start,
163 end: slot.end,
164 releaseAt: offerExpiresAt,
165 isSeat: !!seatsPerTimeSlot,
166 });
167 await this.deps.scheduleOfferExpiry(entry.id, offerExpiresAt);
168 await this.deps.sendOfferEmail({
169 name: entry.name,
170 email: entry.email,
171 timeZone: entry.timeZone,
172 eventTitle: eventType.title,
173 offerStart: slot.start,
174 offerExpiresAt,
175 claimUrl: `${this.deps.webappUrl}/api/waitlist/claim?uid=${entry.uid}`,
176 leaveUrl: `${this.deps.webappUrl}/api/waitlist/leave?uid=${entry.uid}`,
177 });
178 } catch (error) {
179 // Undo the offer so the task's retry offers the seat to this same person instead of the next one
180 await repo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
181 await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, null);
182 throw error;
183 }
184 offered.push(entry.id);
185 }
186 return offered;
```

```text
335 /**
336  * Interleaves booked times (as ISO strings) with open slots in time order, skipping times that are still open.
337  * A full seated slot that can be waitlisted is replaced by its booked time.
338  */
339 const mergeByTime = (
340   slots: Slot[],
341   bookedTimes: string[],
342   seatsPerTimeSlot?: number | null
343 ): (Slot | string)[] => {
344   if (!bookedTimes.length) return slots;
345   const bookedSet = new Set(bookedTimes.map((time) => dayjs(time).valueOf()));
346   const shown = slots.filter(
347     (slot) => !(isSeatedSlotFull(slot, seatsPerTimeSlot) && bookedSet.has(dayjs(slot.time).valueOf()))
348   );
349   const openTimes = new Set(shown.map((slot) => dayjs(slot.time).valueOf()));
350   const booked = bookedTimes.filter((time) => !openTimes.has(dayjs(time).valueOf()));
351   const timeOf = (item: Slot | string) => dayjs(typeof item === "string" ? item : item.time).valueOf();
352   return [...shown, ...booked].sort((a, b) => timeOf(a) - timeOf(b));
353 };

90    * For seated events, only times with every seat booked.
91    */
92   async getBookedTimes(input: { eventTypeId: number; from: Date; to: Date }): Promise<Date[]> {
93     const earliest = new Date(this.now() + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
94     const from = input.from > earliest ? input.from : earliest;
95     if (from >= input.to) return [];
96     const range = { eventTypeId: input.eventTypeId, from, to: input.to };
97     const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
98     const seats = (await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(input.eventTypeId))?.seatsPerTimeSlot;
99     if (!seats) return repo.findActiveBookingStartTimes(range);
100 
101     const attendeesByTime = new Map<number, number>();
102     for (const { startTime, attendees } of await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeCounts(range)) {
103       attendeesByTime.set(startTime.getTime(), (attendeesByTime.get(startTime.getTime()) ?? 0) + attendees);
104     }
105     return [...attendeesByTime]
106       .filter(([, attendees]) => attendees >= seats)
107       .map(([time]) => new Date(time));
108   }
109 
110   /**
111    * Seats at `time` not taken by a booking or a live offer. A non-seated event is one seat, taken by any booking.
112    * Offers whose waitlister already booked are counted only as bookings.
113    */
114   private async countOpenSeats(eventTypeId: number, time: Date, seatsPerTimeSlot: number | null) {
115     const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
116     const bookedEmails = await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt({ eventTypeId, startTime: time });
117     const booked = new Set(bookedEmails ?? []);
118     const bookedSeats = seatsPerTimeSlot ? (bookedEmails?.length ?? 0) : bookedEmails ? 1 : 0;
119     const offers = await repo.findOfferedForTime({ eventTypeId, time });
120     const now = this.now();
121     const liveOffers = offers.filter(
122       (offer) =>
123         !!offer.offerExpiresAt &&
124         offer.offerExpiresAt.getTime() > now &&
125         !booked.has(offer.email.toLowerCase())
126     ).length;
127     return { open: (seatsPerTimeSlot ?? 1) - bookedSeats - liveOffers, booked };
128   }
129
```

```bash
import json, sys, collections
r = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
counts = collections.Counter()
rows = []
for path, f in r["files"].items():
    src = f["source"].splitlines()
    for m in f["mutants"]:
        counts[m["status"]] += 1
        if m["status"] in ("Survived", "NoCoverage"):
            s, e = m["location"]["start"], m["location"]["end"]
            line = src[s["line"] - 1]
            orig = line[s["column"] - 1:] if s["line"] != e["line"] else line[s["column"] - 1:e["column"] - 1]
            rows.append((m["status"], path.split("/")[-1], s["line"], m["mutatorName"], orig.strip()[:70], (m.get("replacement") or "")[:70]))
print(dict(counts), "total", sum(counts.values()))
k = counts["Killed"] + counts["Timeout"]
valid = k + counts["Survived"] + counts["NoCoverage"]
cov = k + counts["Survived"]
print("score %.2f%%  covered %.2f%%" % (100 * k / valid, 100 * k / cov if cov else 0))
for row in sorted(rows, key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1], x[2])):
    print(" | ".join(map(str, row)))
EOF
sleep 60; tail -5 /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lexzach-Documents-Git-cal-diy/16ab1b4a-aa82-4c21-a2fa-dbcafecc04a9/scratchpad/before.log
```

```bash
cd /home/lexzach/Documents/Git/cal.diy; cat > vitest.stryker-154.config.mts <<'EOF'
import path from "node:path";
import baseConfig from "./vitest.config.mts";

// Mutation testing for issue #154 (see stryker.154.config.mjs). Stryker's `related` mode would also run every
// test that imports handleCancelBooking or AvailableTimes, including slow, unrelated booking suites, so the
// tests that exercise this issue's code are listed explicitly instead.
// handleSeats.test.ts's "Correct parameters being passed" tests spy on the handleSeats module's default export,
// which fails inside Stryker's instrumented sandbox (it passes under plain Vitest). They don't touch this issue's
// code, and a failing test stops Stryker before it mutates anything, so they are excluded by name.
const baseAliases = Array.isArray(baseConfig.resolve?.alias) ? baseConfig.resolve.alias : [];

export default {
  ...baseConfig,
  resolve: {
    ...baseConfig.resolve,
    alias: [
      // The sandbox reuses the repo's node_modules, where @calcom/features links back to the original, unmutated
      // packages/features. Without this, code imported as @calcom/features/... is never mutated (false "no coverage").
      { find: /^@calcom\/features(?=\/|$)/, replacement: path.resolve(__dirname, "packages/features") },
      ...baseAliases,
    ],
  },
  test: {
    ...baseConfig.test,
    include: [
      "packages/features/waitlist/services/WaitlistService.test.ts",
      "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/test/handleSeats.test.ts",
      "apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.test.tsx",
    ],
    testNamePattern: /^(?!handleSeats Correct parameters being passed)/,
  },
};
EOF
TZ=UTC timeout 600 node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.stryker-154.config.mts 2>&1 | tail -5
```

```text
      performance.mark("Start");

      let result: T | undefined;
      if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" || !endpointRoute) {
        result = await f(tracedReq, res);
      } else {
        const { wrapApiHandlerWithSentry } = await import("@sentry/nextjs");
        result = await wrapApiHandlerWithSentry(f, endpointRoute)(tracedReq, res);
      }

      ok = true;
      if (result && !res.writableEnded) {
        res.setHeader("X-Trace-Id", traceContext.traceId);
        return res.json(result);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      tracingLogger.error(`${operation} request failed`, safeStringify(err));
      const tracedError = TracedError.createFromError(err, traceContext);
      let error: HttpError;
      if (isTRPCErrorLike(err)) {
        const statusCode = getHTTPStatusCodeFromTRPCErrorLike(err);
        error = new HttpError({ statusCode, message: err.message });
      } else {
        error = getServerErrorFromUnknown(tracedError);
      }
      // we don't want to report Bad Request errors to Sentry / console
      if (!(error.statusCode >= 400 && error.statusCode < 500)) {
        console.error(error);
        const { captureException } = await import("@sentry/nextjs");
        captureException(tracedError);
      }
      res.setHeader("X-Trace-Id", tracedError.traceId);
      return res
        .status(error.statusCode)
        .json({ message: error.message, url: error.url, method: error.method, data: error?.data || null });
    } finally {
      performance.mark("End");
      performance.measure(`[${ok ? "OK" : "ERROR"}][$1] ${req.method} '${req.url}'`, "Start", "End");
    }
  };
}
/**
 * It stringifies the object which is necessary to ensure that in a logging system(like Axiom) we see the object in context in a single log event
 */
export function safeStringify(obj: unknown) {
  try {
    if (obj instanceof Error) {
      // Errors don't serialize well, so we extract what we want
      // We stringify so that we can log the error message and stack trace in a single log event
      return JSON.stringify(obj.stack ?? obj.message);
    }
    // Avoid crashing on circular references
    return JSON.stringify(obj);
  } catch (e) {
    return obj;
  }
}
```

```typescript
  };

  const from = new Date("2026-11-03T00:00:00Z");
  const to = new Date("2026-11-04T00:00:00Z");

  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.resetAllMocks();
    repository = new WaitlistRepository(prismaClient as unknown as PrismaClient);
  });

  it("finds the offers made for one time of one event type, with what's needed to tell if they are live", async () => {
    const time = new Date("2026-11-03T10:00:00Z");
    const offers = [{ email: "a@x.com", offerExpiresAt: new Date("2026-11-03T04:00:00Z") }];
    prismaClient.waitlistEntry.findMany.mockResolvedValue(offers);

    await expect(repository.findOfferedForTime({ eventTypeId: 7, time })).resolves.toEqual(offers);
    expect(prismaClient.waitlistEntry.findMany).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      where: { eventTypeId: 7, status: WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, offerStart: time },
      select: { email: true, offerExpiresAt: true },
    });
  });

  it("counts attendees of the event type's active bookings in the range, oldest first", async () => {
    const startTime = new Date("2026-11-03T10:00:00Z");
    prismaClient.booking.findMany.mockResolvedValue([{ startTime, _count: { attendees: 2 } }]);

    await expect(
      repository.findActiveBookingAttendeeCounts({ eventTypeId: 7, from, to })
    ).resolves.toEqual([{ startTime, attendees: 2 }]);
    expect(prismaClient.booking.findMany).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      where: {
        eventTypeId: 7,
        startTime: { gte: from, lt: to },
        status: { in: [BookingStatus.ACCEPTED, BookingStatus.PENDING] },
      },
      select: { startTime: true, _count: { select: { attendees: true } } },
      orderBy: { startTime: "asc" },
    });
  });

  it("loads the event type's seat count", async () => {
    await repository.findEventTypeForWaitlist(7);
    expect(prismaClient.eventType.findUnique).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({
        where: { id: 7 },
        select: expect.objectContaining({ seatsPerTimeSlot: true }),
      })
    );
  });

  it("creates a hold as a single seat when asked to", async () => {
    await repository.createSlotHold({
      uid: "entry",
      eventTypeId: 7,
      userId: 9,
      start: from,
      end: to,
      releaseAt: to,
      isSeat: true,
    });
    expect(prismaClient.selectedSlots.create).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      data: expect.objectContaining({ uid: "waitlist:entry", isSeat: true }),
    });
  });
});
```

```typescript
import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from "next";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

const { createBooking, releaseHoldAfterBooking, log } = vi.hoisted(() => {
  const log: Record<string, ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>> = {};
  const logger = new Proxy(log, {
    get: (target, prop: string) => {
      if (prop === "getSubLogger") return () => logger;
      target[prop] ??= vi.fn();
      return target[prop];
    },
  });
  return { createBooking: vi.fn(), releaseHoldAfterBooking: vi.fn(), log: logger };
});

vi.mock("@calcom/lib/logger", () => ({ default: log }));
vi.mock("@sentry/nextjs", () => ({ wrapApiHandlerWithSentry: (handler: unknown) => handler }));
vi.mock("@calcom/features/auth/lib/getServerSession", () => ({ getServerSession: async () => null }));
vi.mock("@calcom/features/bookings/di/RegularBookingService.container", () => ({
  getRegularBookingService: () => ({ createBooking }),
}));
vi.mock("@calcom/features/bot-detection", () => ({
  BotDetectionService: class {
    checkBotDetection = async () => undefined;
  },
}));
vi.mock("@calcom/features/eventtypes/repositories/eventTypeRepository", () => ({
  EventTypeRepository: class {},
}));
vi.mock("@calcom/features/flags/features.repository", () => ({ FeaturesRepository: class {} }));
vi.mock("@calcom/lib/checkRateLimitAndThrowError", () => ({ checkRateLimitAndThrowError: async () => undefined }));
vi.mock("@calcom/prisma", () => ({ prisma: {} }));
vi.mock("@calcom/features/waitlist/services/getWaitlistService", () => ({
  getWaitlistService: () => ({ releaseHoldAfterBooking }),
}));

const start = "2026-11-03T10:00:00.000Z";

const book = async (cookies: Record<string, string>) => {
  const { default: handler } = await import("./event");
  const req = {
    method: "POST",
    url: "/api/book/event",
    headers: {},
    cookies,
    body: { eventTypeId: 1, start },
  } as unknown as NextApiRequest;
  const res = {
    writableEnded: false,
    setHeader: vi.fn(),
    status: vi.fn().mockReturnThis(),
    json: vi.fn(),
  };
  await handler(req, res as unknown as NextApiResponse);
  return res;
};

describe("POST /api/book/event waitlist hold release", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    createBooking.mockResolvedValue({ uid: "booking-uid" });
    releaseHoldAfterBooking.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  });

  it("releases the hold of the waitlist offer the booker claimed", async () => {
    const res = await book({ uid: "entry-uid" });

    expect(releaseHoldAfterBooking).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      uid: "entry-uid",
      eventTypeId: 1,
      start: new Date(start),
    });
    expect(res.json).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ uid: "booking-uid" });
  });

  it("does not look for a waitlist hold when the booker has no claim cookie", async () => {
    await book({});
    expect(releaseHoldAfterBooking).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("still returns the booking, and logs the error, when releasing the hold fails", async () => {
    releaseHoldAfterBooking.mockRejectedValue(new Error("db down"));

    const res = await book({ uid: "entry-uid" });

    expect(res.json).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ uid: "booking-uid" });
    expect(res.status).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(log.error).toHaveBeenCalledWith("Error releasing waitlist hold", expect.stringContaining("db down"));
  });
});
```

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #154 -- Multi seat event waitlist

**PR(s):** #TBD (from `feat/issue-154-multi-seat-waitlist`)  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner  **Config:** [stryker.154.config.mjs](../../../stryker.154.config.mjs) + [vitest.stryker-154.config.mts](../../../vitest.stryker-154.config.mts), built on the shared [stryker.config.mjs](../../../stryker.config.mjs) by @zach-short  **Command:** `STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/154-zachbowden-<before|after>.json TZ=UTC node_modules/.bin/stryker run stryker.154.config.mjs` (Node 22)
**Reports:** [before](reports/154-zachbowden-before.json) · [after](reports/154-zachbowden-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 70.73% → after 97.04% (covered mutants only: 85.80% → 98.01%)

### Setup notes

- **Only the lines this PR added or changed are mutated.** `stryker.154.config.mjs` lists them as line ranges in `WaitlistService.ts`, `WaitlistRepository.ts`, `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `pages/api/book/event.ts` and `AvailableTimes.tsx`. A single line has to be written as a range (`:120-120`); `:120` alone matches no file and is silently skipped.
- **The test list is explicit.** `vitest.stryker-154.config.mts` names this PR's test files. `related: true` would also run every suite that imports `handleCancelBooking` or `AvailableTimes`.
- **Three pre-existing tests are excluded by name.** The "Correct parameters being passed into handleSeats" tests in `handleSeats.test.ts` spy on the `handleSeats` module's default export. They pass under plain Vitest but fail in Stryker's instrumented sandbox, and a failing test stops Stryker before it mutates anything. They don't run any of this PR's code, so `testNamePattern` skips them.
- **`@calcom/features` is aliased into the sandbox (false "no coverage").** Stryker's sandbox reuses the repo's `node_modules`, where `@calcom/features` is a relative link back to the *original* `packages/features`. `handleSeats.test.ts` imports `handleCancelBooking` as `@calcom/features/...`, so it ran the unmutated file. My first run reported all 14 `handleCancelBooking.ts` mutants as no coverage, even though the seat-cancel tests ran. The Vitest config now aliases `@calcom/features` to the sandbox's own `packages/features`. The committed before report is from the corrected run, so the before/after comparison only changes the tests.
- **Mutant counts differ by 2 between runs.** The new route test found a logging bug (see the table below). Fixing it removed the `{ error }` object at `event.ts:74` and `handleCancelBooking.ts:85`, and with it one ObjectLiteral mutant each. Every other mutant is at the same location in both reports.

**Bug found:** while writing `event.test.ts › still returns the booking, and logs the error, when releasing the hold fails`, the log assertion failed. `safeStringify({ error })` logged `{"error":{}}`, because an `Error` inside an object serializes to `{}` and the message and stack are lost. `safeStringify(error)` handles errors directly. I fixed this in `event.ts` and in the moved `queueWaitlistOffers` helper in `handleCancelBooking.ts`.

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

They showed three things. First, my fake repository was too forgiving: it ignored its arguments and returned the same bookings for any time. So nothing checked that the service asks about the *right* time. Two survivors (`{ eventTypeId, startTime }` → `{}`) passed only because of that. Second, I had only tested states where data exists. Nothing covered a seated time with zero bookings (both when joining and after the last attendee cancels), an event type deleted while a task is pending, or an unknown event type on the public booked-times endpoint. Each one would have been a crash, not a wrong answer. Third, my UI tests checked *what* appears but not *where*. Eight sort-order mutants survived because no test checked that the waitlist button sits at its own time among the slots. The no-coverage mutants added a fourth point: the repository's real queries and the booking route's hold release had no tests at all. Testing the route then exposed a real logging bug.

**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**

Not in the existing assertions; the survivors came from missing cases, not wrong expected values. But `WaitlistService.ts:134` made me check where my expected value came from. My existing test ("does not offer slots starting less than 6 hours from now") used a slot 5 hours away, which passes under both `<` and `<=`. The requirement is issue #13's "closer than 6 hours out" (and #154's "six-hour rules remain unchanged"). Under that rule, exactly 6 hours is *not* excluded, so the new test expects an offer there. For the deleted-event-type and unknown-event-type tests, neither issue gives an expected value. Their expected results ("no offer", "no times", "the entry leaves `OFFERED`") come from the general rule that a background task or public endpoint must not crash on missing data, not from what my code returns. Similarly, the repository test's `ACCEPTED`/`PENDING` filter comes from #13's existing definition of an active booking (`findActiveBookingStartTimes`), not from copying the new query.

**3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**

I used Claude Code (log linked from the PR).

- **Configuration:** it wrote `stryker.154.config.mjs` and `vitest.stryker-154.config.mts` from @zach-short's shared config and my #138 setup, limited to this PR's changed lines.
- **Running:** Stryker failed twice before mutating:
  - single-line ranges like `:120` matched no file, so they had to be written as `:120-120`;
  - three pre-existing `handleSeats` spy tests fail in the sandbox, so they are excluded by name.
- **False "no coverage":** the first successful run reported 0% coverage for `handleCancelBooking.ts`, even though the cancel tests ran. Claude traced this to the sandbox resolving `@calcom/features` to the original files through `node_modules` and added the alias. The committed before report is from that corrected run (the uncorrected run scored 65.85%).
- **Analysis and tests:** it drafted the classification of the 24 survivors and the new tests. One of those tests caught the `safeStringify({ error })` logging bug, which was fixed in the same change.
- **What I verified:**
  - all selected tests pass on the unmutated code (70 passed, 3 skipped by the name filter);
  - every "killed after" mutant shows as Killed in the after report (compared mutant by mutant: file, line, column, mutator, replacement);
  - the only mutants missing from the after report are the 2 removed by the logging fix;
  - the scores match Stryker's own summary (70.73% / 85.80% before, 97.04% / 98.01% after);
  - each equivalent classification holds for every reachable state (for example, that only `WAITING` → `OFFERED` sets the `OFFERED` status, and it always sets `offerStart`).
```
